The History

From the dorm rooms of CPI to the "American Dream" jackpot. The story of a family who fought the industry and won.

1985-1992: The Ironheads & The Cold War

The story begins at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in Blacksburg. The five members (O'Connells and Wrights) formed a protective, insular unit—a "fortress"—to survive the academic and social pressures of the Class of '89.

After an Apex Records A&R scout heard their 1986 CPI student contest cassette track “Ignition”, Apex signed the group—releasing Electric Color (1987) and Neon Hearts (1989) across a five-year “Cold War” over the band's identity. Apex wanted a pop band; The Stardust Engine wanted to be industrial rockers. This era was defined by "malicious compliance," hiding dark lyrics inside polished pop songs.

1992: The "Friction" Catastrophe

The Day The Contract Ended

In September 1992, to isolate the band from Blacksburg while tracking their third project Friction, Apex leased a gated mansion in Beverly Hills (charging 100% of the $25,000/month rent back against the band's recoupable royalties). With twenty slick marble front steps and zero wheelchair ramps—forcing Evan and Tyler to carry Ryan's wheelchair up and down the stairs daily—freeway smog, and paparazzi, the family hated every second of it because it wasn't Blacksburg and it wasn't home. Then, at the October 14, 1992 photo shoot, Apex executive Julian Vance attempted to exploit the sibling bond between Ryan and Cassidy for a coerced, sexualized marketing campaign. The resulting confrontation—the "Dirty Mirror" incident—ended with Holly O'Connell (then a law student) forcing the label to void the contract.

The band was free, but they were blacklisted and broke. This marked the beginning of "The Wilderness Years."

1996: The "American Dream" Event

Daleville, VA (The Gas Station)

Late one night, returning from a gig in Lexington, the band stopped at a gas station in Daleville for snacks. Cassidy O'Connell bought a "Quick Pick" lottery ticket on a whim. She liked the visual pattern of the numbers.

The next morning, reading the newspaper over breakfast, she realized she had matched every single number for the American Dream Jackpot.

"She didn't scream. She just handed the ticket to Holly and said, 'Build us a fortress.'"

Jackpot Total: $2.04 Billion.

1997-Present: The "Loss Leader" Era

With the trust fund secured, the band ceased to be a commercial entity and became a "Loss Leader" for the family empire.

  • 1997: Released Hard Reset, their first album with an "infinite budget."
  • 2000: Founded Mirage (their own subsidiary label).
  • Today: They tour when they want, record what they want, and answer to no one.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
